entry:seoul-commit.note: Link resolves to the UK Government text of the commitments. Name, Layer 5, mu, pow 1 (voluntary firm commitments) and active status match; the page was last substantively updated on 7 Feb 2025.

entry:seoul-commit:desc.note: 16 original signatories confirmed; four more were added on 7 Feb 2025 (20 in total).

entry:seoul-commit:context.note: Halting commitment (IV) and voluntary nature confirmed. The UK is not among the signatories' home countries; the government describes them as spanning North America, Asia, Europe and the Middle East. The SB 53 / RAISE causal sentence is analytic.

entry:seoul-commit:cov:halt.note: Halting commitment (IV) and voluntary nature confirmed. The UK is not among the signatories' home countries; the government describes them as spanning North America, Asia, Europe and the Middle East. The SB 53 / RAISE causal sentence is analytic.

entry:seoul-commit:cov.note: acct, eval, halt and thresh are supported; commitment III and the preamble also cover mitigations and weight security, which the set omits.

entry:seoul-commit:cov:eval.note: Commitment I (pre-deployment assessment, internal and external evaluations as appropriate) and II (assess whether thresholds are breached) match the eval note. VII (public transparency) and the 16 May 2024 signatories match the acct note.

entry:seoul-commit:cov:acct.note: Commitment I (pre-deployment assessment, internal and external evaluations as appropriate) and II (assess whether thresholds are breached) match the eval note. VII (public transparency) and the 16 May 2024 signatories match the acct note.

entry:seoul-commit:cov:thresh.note: Factual core checked: commitment II requires thresholds at which severe risks would be intolerable, defined using capabilities among other factors (footnote 3), and IV the actions if they are met. The government calls the agreement a 'world-first'. 'Catalyst for what became the lab-published-framework norm' cannot be checked.

entry:hiroshima:desc.note: Code of Conduct (Oct 2023) with 11 actions confirmed; reporting framework launched 7 Feb 2025 (pilot 2024), not 2024.

entry:hiroshima:cov:update.note: Code of Conduct (Oct 2023) with 11 actions confirmed; reporting framework launched 7 Feb 2025 (pilot 2024), not 2024.

entry:hiroshima:context.note: Code topics (risk identification, security, transparency, content authentication, incident reporting) confirmed in actions 1–7. v2.0 launch on 28 May 2026 for SMEs confirmed. New fact: v2.0 reports from 31 companies published 2 Oct 2026. The 50+ pledges are organisations, not only companies. The Seoul comparison is analytic.

entry:hiroshima:cov.note: Action 1 (identify, evaluate, mitigate risks across the lifecycle, incl. red-teaming), action 6 (security incl. model weights, insider threats), action 11 (data inputs), actions 2 and 7 (post-deployment misuse, content authentication) and actions 3–4 (transparency reports, incident sharing) support the notes. Reports are invited annually and contribute to OECD monitoring. Compared with the GPAI Code's Appendix 3, Hiroshima is indeed less prescriptive on evaluation method.

entry:gpai-cop:context.note: Three chapters, safety only for systemic-risk models, drafting by independent experts facilitated by the AI Office, and publication on 10 Jul 2025 are confirmed. Signing is voluntary and the Commission and AI Board found it adequate. Meta is absent from the Commission's signatory list (7 Oct 2026); its refusal is documented only secondarily (TechCrunch quoting Kaplan).
entry:gpai-cop:context.missing: A primary Meta or Commission statement that Meta declined. Joel Kaplan's LinkedIn post (Jul 2025) returned HTTP 429. 'Only vetted route' and 'open question' are interpretive.

edge:gpai-cop|meta-faif.note: The Commission list (7 Oct 2026) confirms Meta is not a signatory. That it 'declined' comes only from a secondary report quoting Meta's chief global affairs officer.
edge:gpai-cop|meta-faif.missing: Primary Meta statement (Kaplan LinkedIn post, Jul 2025; blocked with HTTP 429) or a Commission statement naming Meta.

entry:gpai-cop:cov.note: All eight listed elements are supported; timing (trigger points, pre-market Framework and Model Report) is also covered but missing.

entry:gpai-cop:cov:thresh.note: Measure 4.1 tiers are signatory-defined and capability-based; the 10^25 FLOP figure is the Act's classification presumption, which the Code does not address.

entry:gpai-cop:cov:elicit.note: Elicitation is mandated (Appendix 3.2); red-teaming is an example method; external evaluation is required with two exceptions (Appendix 3.5).

entry:gpai-cop:cov:sec.note: Commitment 6 and Appendix 4 confirmed; no supply-chain measures in the text.

entry:gpai-cop:cov:update.note: AI Office reviews at least every two years (Q&A updated 20 Jul 2026); no revision of the Jul 2025 text found.

entry:gpai-cop:cov:eval.note: Measure 3.2 requires at least state-of-the-art model evaluations as specified in Appendix 3. Objective A ties the Code to demonstrating compliance with Articles 53 and 55, which supports the 'operational bridge' description.

edge:gpai-cop|eu-aia.note: Voluntary tool; Commission and AI Board confirmed adequacy; signatories can show compliance by adhering.

edge:gpai-cop|eu-aio.note: AI Office facilitated drafting, chairs the Signatory Taskforce and reviews the Code at least every two years.
